cohort: The study included 340 nulliparous women with a singleton fetus in cephalic presentation who underwent cervical ripening at term (>=37 weeks) for maternal and/or fetal disease.
finding: Nulliparous women who required repeated methods for cervical ripening at term reported significantly worse experiences of ripening and childbirth in the immediate postpartum period compared to those who received PG, CRB, or M used alone.
mod_finding: The association between repeated cervical ripening methods and worse experiences of ripening and childbirth was found regardless of the mode of delivery.
